bank_name: PLACEHOLDER - German Composite Bank (identity not confirmed)
bank_name_note: Same situation as BANK011: this is the Statlog German Credit dataset (Prof. Hans Hofmann, Universitat Hamburg, 1994) - an academic benchmark, not tied to a named real institution. Generic placeholder identity, consistent with BANK011's resolution.
source_description: 1,000-row installment-loan applicant dataset (UCI/Statlog German Credit Data). Demographics, credit-bureau-style history, and loan terms (amount, duration, purpose), with a real binary outcome column (target). Human-readable categorical labels (already decoded from the original A11/A12-style codes).
profiling_method: Direct read via pandas: 0 nulls across all 21 columns, value_counts() on every categorical, groupby(col)['target'].mean() for risk-ordering and polarity checks, cross-checked target's 700/300 split against the dataset's well-documented published good/bad split to confirm target=1 means default (not inverted).

mappings.notes: 0% missing, 700/300 split matches the dataset's well-known published good/bad counts - confirms target=1=default, not inverted.

mappings.formula: Rank purpose's 10 categories by observed target rate (out-of-fold, train-only), ascending risk, assign 1..10.
mappings.notes: Genuine existing-canonical-field match - this dataset has a real loan-purpose concept, unlike BANK010/BANK011.

mappings.formula: Rank housing's 3 categories (own/rent/for free) by observed target rate, ascending risk, assign 1..3.
Rank job's 4 categories by observed target rate, ascending risk, assign 1..4.

mappings.notes: Genuine existing-canonical-field match, already an integer count at this bank.

mappings.formula: num_dependents = people_liable (source values are 1='0 to 2 dependents', 2='3 or more' - a bucketed proxy, not a literal headcount)
mappings.notes: FLAGGED: the source field itself is only 2 buckets (1 or 2), not a real count - do not treat num_dependents as a precise headcount for this bank, it is a coarse proxy.
Genuine existing-canonical-field match, unit-converted from years to months.

mappings.formula: years_employed = band midpoint: '< 1 year'->0.5, '1<=..<4 years'->2.5, '4<=..<7 years'->5.5, '>=7 years'->10.0, 'unemployed'->0.0
mappings.notes: Source is categorical bands, not a continuous value - midpoint approximation, standard practice but not a literal figure. '>=7 years' open-ended band arbitrarily anchored at 10.0.

derived_fields.notes: Maps onto an EXISTING canonical field. Only the single 'delay in past' category is treated as a genuine prior-default signal - 'critical account / other credits elsewhere' is NOT included here (it's a different concept, existing debt elsewhere, not necessarily delinquency).

new_generic_fields.notes: 4 categories, out-of-fold risk-ordered. Real, non-obvious signal: 'no checking account' has the LOWEST observed default rate (11.7%) despite sounding negative, '< 0 DM' (overdrawn) has the highest (49.3%) - the encoding captures this correctly since it ranks by observed rate, not by intuition. This asymmetry is a documented characteristic of this dataset, not a data error.

5 categories, out-of-fold risk-ordered. CAVEAT: two categories that sound like good history ('no credits/all paid duly' n=40, 'all credits at this bank paid duly' n=49) show the HIGHEST default rates (62.5%, 57.1%) in this sample - almost certainly small-sample noise (tiny n) rather than a real reversed relationship. Flagging so this isn't mistaken for a data quality bug later.

new_generic_fields.formula: requested_loan_amount_usd = (credit_amount_dm / 1.95583) / fx_rate_eur_per_usd - DM->EUR via the official fixed ECB conversion rate (exact, not an estimate), then EUR->USD via country_macro.DEU.fx_rate_per_usd
new_generic_fields.notes: Distinct concept from BANK011's credit_limit (a revolving facility size) - this is a specific installment loan amount requested, new generic field name reflects that.

Source is already an ordinal 1-4 band ('installment as % of disposable income', banded not literal) - kept as the ordinal band, NOT force-mapped onto foir since the literal fraction isn't known, only which quartile-ish band.
4 categories, out-of-fold risk-ordered - Five C's 'Collateral' adjacent signal.
3 categories (none/bank/stores), out-of-fold risk-ordered. Conceptually adjacent to other_lender_emi_ratio but not a literal ratio - kept as its own new field rather than force-mapped.
Weak, dated signal (1990s-era proxy) - brought in per 'don't lose information upfront', not expected to carry much weight.
Genuinely new concept (loan tenor) - no existing canonical field for this.

compliance_flagged_fields.target_fields: gender_enc + marital_status_enc (BOTH REUSED from BANK011's schema addition, not new columns)
compliance_flagged_fields.formula: Parsed from the combined field: 'male: single'->gender=1,marital=single; 'male: married/widowed'->gender=1,marital=married_or_widowed; 'male: divorced/separated'->gender=1,marital=divorced_or_separated; 'female: divorced/separated/married'->gender=2,marital=UNKNOWN (source does not distinguish female marital sub-status - a genuine, documented limitation of this dataset, not an onboarding error)
compliance_flagged_fields.confidence: low for the female marital sub-status specifically
compliance_flagged_fields.notes: COMPLIANCE FLAG, same as BANK011: gender_enc must not be added to FEATURE_COLS without explicit review. This field is ALSO a well-known point of criticism of this exact dataset (conflating sex and marital status, and only distinguishing marital status for men) - worth being aware of if this dataset is ever cited in any external-facing analysis.

NEW COMPLIANCE FLAG (added to ml_models/trainer.py's COMPLIANCE_EXCLUDED_COLS by this onboarding): national-origin-adjacent protected characteristic. CONFIRMED CORRELATED WITH TARGET in this sample - default rate 30.7% for foreign workers vs 10.8% for non-foreign (n=37) - exactly the kind of correlation fair-lending law exists to keep out of underwriting models. Excluded from auto-discovery by default, same mechanism as gender_enc.

unmapped_required_fields_note: No income, CIBIL/bureau-score, geography, or macro-trend fields exist in this dataset. Notably richer than BANK011 on loan-structure fields (purpose, duration, amount, existing credits) but has no revolving-credit behavioral history the way BANK011 does.
currency_conversion: credit_amount is DM (Deutsche Mark, pre-Euro). Converted DM->EUR via the official fixed ECB conversion rate (1 EUR = 1.95583 DM, exact historical fact, not an estimate), then EUR->USD via country_macro.DEU.fx_rate_per_usd (disclosed estimate). Real Earth's canonical monetary unit is USD, same convention as BANK010/BANK011.
onboarding_scope_decision: TRAINING-ONLY, same default applied without re-asking (consistent with BANK011's confirmed preference) - flagging this explicitly since credit_amount/months_duration together could plausibly support a broader scope (real installment-loan terms exist here), same as BANK011's LIMIT_BAL fork. Revisit if this default should change.
bank_identity_decision: PLACEHOLDER - 'German Composite Bank', same treatment as BANK011.
feature_cols_decision: Same as BANK011 - new columns are NOT auto-added to FEATURE_COLS, but ARE eligible for run_training()'s bank-scoped auto-discovery (except foreign_worker_flag/gender_enc/marital_status_enc, which require include_compliance_excluded=True).
world_assignment: Real Earth ('real'), same quarantine rules as BANK010/BANK011.
